fml.menu.mods.info.description.starrysky: A more beautiful night sky: more stars, varied sizes and colors, gentle twinkling and shooting stars. Client-side only.
starrysky.configuration.title: Starry Sky Configuration
starrysky.configuration.enabled.tooltip: Turns the improved night sky on or off.
starrysky.configuration.starCount.toolti: Number of stars on the celestial sphere. Vanilla shows about 800. The Milky Way adds twice as many tiny stars on top. Even 10000 stays cheap to draw.
starrysky.configuration.starSize.tooltip: Size multiplier applied to every star.
starrysky.configuration.coloredStars.too: Adds subtle color variations: white, bluish and pale yellow stars.
starrysky.configuration.twinkle.tooltip: Makes the stars gently twinkle over time.
starrysky.configuration.shootingStars.to: Occasional shooting stars streak across the night sky.
starrysky.configuration.shootingStarFreq: Average number of shooting stars per minute on a clear night. 0 disables them.
starrysky.configuration.milkyWay.tooltip: A glowing band of star dust crosses the night sky. This is the most demanding effect of the mod, although still light: turn it off first if the game slows down when you look at the night sky.
starrysky.configuration.auroras.tooltip: Curtains of green and violet light dance in the northern sky at night, only in cold biomes (snow, ice).
starrysky.configuration.telescope.toolti: Aim a spyglass at a bright star at night to see its name and characteristics.
starrysky.telescope.hint.too_bright: The sky is too bright to see the stars
starrysky.configuration.hideVanillaStars: Hides Minecraft's original stars wherever Starry Sky is active.
starrysky.configuration.dimensions.toolt: Dimension IDs where Starry Sky is active (e.g. minecraft:overworld). Only dimensions with a normal sky are affected: the Nether and the End stay unchanged.
